column1: # controls.tsv (harbor#950) — every control on this box: lint rule, check, admission rule, injection rule, CI gate and Vale rule.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A control is a registry row before it is code (D-62). Rules, checks, admission
# rules and injection rules used to live in five registers with five shapes, so "every control went red
# once", "every control has an owner" and "every control can be switched off" could not be computed across
# engines (09a S2). One row per control states its id, mode, owner and proof; the lint prints rule titles
# from here (`--list`), the self-test refuses a naming rule that did not go red on every surface it
# declares, and promotion from warn to block is a one-cell edit in a person's PR (standards/naming.md
# §10.3). It replaces rules.tsv; docs/reference/checks.md stays hand-kept until a generator reads this file.
# An id found in the tree and absent here is red (name.control-unregistered): registers.tsv names where
# each type of control is found.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> mode <TAB> type <TAB> engine <TAB> surfaces <TAB> moment <TAB> function <TAB> stability
#   id         <family>.<slug>, a family or lint subject first (D-10); permanent, never reused (D-19)
#   mode       shadow | warn | block (D-29, D-64). shadow records and prints nothing, warn prints, block
#              fails the run. A control is born warn; block needs a person's PR after the control went red
#              and ran 4 weeks with no finding accepted as false. advisory and inform are legacy spellings
#              of warn (terms.tsv, class mode): the lint reads them as warn and no row here uses them.
#   type       lint | check | admission | injection | ci | vale (terms.tsv, class control-type); the
#              register that resolves `<type>:<id>` is the row of that name in registers.tsv
#   engine     the file that evaluates the control; - when nothing evaluates it yet
#   surfaces   the surfaces.tsv ids a naming rule judges, comma-separated; - for every other control.
#              --self-test fails unless the rule goes red on each one
#   moment     write | commit | ci | merge | deploy | runtime | schedule | event | manual (class moment; D-89)
#   stability  experimental | stable | deprecated; a deprecated row names its successor (D-19)
#   owner      the family that answers for it (terms.tsv, class family)
#   red_proof  the suite that watched the control go red, read from LINT_REDLOG while that suite passed
#              (bin/lint-rule-health.sh does the same); - when no suite is known to have seen it red
#   emitted    the id the control prints today when it differs from `id`, - otherwise. An admission rule
#              is <guard>:<rule>, a check is its docs/reference/checks.md id, an injection rule is its front-matter id,
#              a CI gate is its check name. The rename wave that retires the old spelling clears the cell
